claims.question: q1
claims.claim: The paper introduces a three-layer enterprise ontology framework consisting of Role, Domain, and Interaction ontologies to ground LLM-based enterprise agents.
claims.quote: We introduce a three-layer ontological framework--Role, Domain, and Interaction ontologies--grounding LLM-based enterprise agents.

claims.question: q1
claims.claim: It formalizes asymmetric neurosymbolic coupling: current enterprise systems constrain agent inputs such as context assembly, tool discovery, and governance thresholds but not outputs, and it proposes extending this to output-side validation including response checking, reasoning verification, and compliance enforcement.
claims.quote: We formalize asymmetric neurosymbolic coupling: current enterprise systems constrain agent inputs (context assembly, tool discovery, governance thresholds) but not outputs, and we propose mechanisms extending this coupling to output-side validation (response checking, reasoning verification, compliance enforcement).

claims.question: q3
claims.claim: In a controlled experiment of 1,800 runs across five industries and three LLMs, ontology-coupled agents significantly outperformed ungrounded agents on Metric Accuracy and Role Consistency with p < .001 across all three models and large effect sizes Kendall's W = .46-.64.
claims.quote: A controlled experiment (1,800 runs across five industries and three LLMs: Claude Sonnet 4, Qwen 2.5 72B, Gemma 4 26B) finds ontology-coupled agents significantly outperform ungrounded agents on Metric Accuracy (p <.001) and Role Consistency (p <.001) across all three models with large effect sizes (Kendall's W = .46-.64).

claims.question: q3
claims.claim: Ontology improvements are greatest where LLM parametric knowledge is weakest, with Vietnam-localized domains showing ontology lift 2x that of English domains.
claims.quote: Improvements are greatest where LLM parametric knowledge is weakest--particularly in Vietnam-localized domains, where ontology lift is 2x that of English domains.

claims.question: q3
claims.claim: The paper reports empirical evidence for an inverse parametric knowledge effect, where ontological grounding value is inversely proportional to LLM training-data coverage of the domain.
claims.quote: (5) empirical evidence for the inverse parametric knowledge effect--ontological grounding value is inversely proportional to LLM training-data coverage of the domain;

claims.question: q4
claims.claim: The paper claims cross-model replication establishing model-independence and a production system serving 22 industry verticals with 650+ agents.
claims.quote: (6) cross-model replication establishing model-independence; (7) a production system serving 22 industry verticals with 650+ agents.

claims.question: q5
claims.claim: Enterprise adoption of LLMs is constrained by hallucination, domain drift, and inability to enforce regulatory compliance at the reasoning level; the paper presents a neurosymbolic architecture in the Foundation AgenticOS (FAOS) platform using ontology-constrained neural reasoning.
claims.quote: Enterprise adoption of Large Language Models (LLMs) is constrained by hallucination, domain drift, and the inability to enforce regulatory compliance at the reasoning level. We present a neurosymbolic architecture implemented within the Foundation AgenticOS (FAOS) platform that addresses these limitations through ontology-constrained neural reasoning.
